documents.title: Purchasing approval thresholds
documents.text:
To: All department heads
From: Finance Department
Subject: Purchasing approval thresholds

With effect from 1 July, the following approval rules apply to all purchases of equipment and services.

Purchases under 500 euros may be approved by the department head. Purchases from 500 to 5,000 euros require the approval of the divisional director. Any purchase above 5,000 euros requires the approval of the Chief Financial Officer and must be supported by quotations from at least three suppliers. Where several identical items are bought together, the total value of the order determines the approval level, not the price of each item.

Purchases may not be divided into smaller orders in order to avoid a threshold. Orders placed without the necessary approval will not be paid, and the department concerned will bear the cost. All purchase requests should be submitted on the standard form, together with the quotations, at least ten working days before the date on which the goods are needed.

documents.title: Request to replace six laptops
documents.text:
To: Finance Department
From: Naledi Dube, Head of Design
Subject: Request to replace six laptops

Dear colleagues,

Six of the laptops used by my team are more than five years old and can no longer run the current version of our design software. I would like to replace them with six identical machines. The supplier whom we have used previously offers them at 1,150 euros each, and has said that it will take 8 percent off the total for an order of six or more. I have obtained two further quotations, for similar machines, from other suppliers, and I attach them to this message. We need the laptops by 15 September for a major client project.

Could you please tell me who must approve the purchase?

Regards,
Naledi Dube

choices: The divisional director
The Chief Financial Officer
The head of the department

questions.explanation: The total of 6,348 euros exceeds 5,000, so the Chief Financial Officer's approval is required, and the memo says it is the total order value that counts.

questions.prompt: Why has Ms. Dube attached two other quotations?
choices: The preferred supplier had refused to give a discount
Orders of this value must have three quotations
The department head must compare all printed prices
The divisional director asked for them in advance
questions.explanation: Purchases above 5,000 euros must be 'supported by quotations from at least three suppliers'.

questions.prompt: What is NOT stated in the memo?
choices: Orders placed without approval will not be paid by Finance
Every purchase needs the Chief Financial Officer
Orders must not be split to avoid a threshold
Requests need ten working days' notice
questions.explanation: Only purchases above 5,000 euros need the Chief Financial Officer's approval; smaller ones go to the department head or the divisional director. The other statements appear in the memo.

questions.prompt: The word "thresholds" in the memo is closest in meaning to
choices: rewards
deadlines
suppliers
limits
questions.explanation: The approval thresholds are the amounts at which a higher level of approval becomes necessary.

documents.title: Leadership Workshop Agenda
documents.text:
LEADERSHIP WORKSHOP | Agenda
Friday 10 October, Conference Room B

9:00 to 9:30 Welcome and introductions
9:30 to 11:00 Session 1: Giving effective feedback
11:00 to 11:15 Break
11:15 to 12:30 Session 2: Managing remote teams
12:30 to 13:30 Lunch (provided; please state dietary requirements at registration)
13:30 to 15:00 Session 3: Handling conflict
15:00 to 15:15 Break
15:15 to 16:30 Session 4: Planning for succession
16:30 to 17:00 Closing discussion and certificates

Facilitator: Dr. Karen Lofgren, Hallam Business School. Participants are asked to bring a laptop or tablet for the group exercises, and to arrive no later than 8:45 in order to collect their name badges. Parking is available at the rear of the building for a fee of 6 euros per day, and the nearest tram stop, Hallam Street, is a three-minute walk from the entrance. Lunch is served in the atrium next to the conference room.

Certificates are awarded only to participants who attend at least three of the four sessions and the closing discussion.

documents.title: Attending the workshop
documents.text:
To: Workshop Coordinator
From: Marek Soltys, Regional Manager
Subject: Attending the workshop

Dear colleague,

I am registered for the leadership workshop on 10 October, but I now have a meeting with a client in the afternoon that I cannot move. The meeting is due to begin at 14:00 and will last about two hours, and I would have to leave the workshop at 13:30 immediately after lunch. I would, however, be able to return for the closing discussion at 16:30. I would still like to earn the certificate if possible, so could you tell me whether I would qualify? I am sorry for the short notice. Also, I am vegetarian and forgot to mention this at registration; I hope this will not cause the caterers any trouble. Please let me know if a written confirmation of my partial attendance is needed.

Marek Soltys

questions.prompt: Would Mr. Soltys qualify for a certificate under the plan he describes?
choices: No, because he would attend only two sessions
Yes, because he would attend the closing discussion
Yes, because the lunch counts as a session
No, because certificates are given only on request
questions.explanation: He would attend Sessions 1 and 2 (before 13:30) and the closing discussion, but a certificate needs at least three of the four sessions as well as the closing discussion.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Mr. Soltys's e-mail?
choices: To cancel his registration for the workshop
To ask the organiser to change the date
To discuss attending despite a clash
To complain about the topics being covered
questions.explanation: He explains that a client meeting clashes with the afternoon and asks whether he could still obtain a certificate.

questions.prompt: Which session or sessions would Mr. Soltys miss?
choices: Session 4 only
Sessions 1 and 2
Sessions 3 and 4
Sessions 2 and 3
questions.explanation: He leaves at 13:30, when Session 3 begins, and returns at 16:30, after Session 4 has finished.

questions.prompt: What does Mr. Soltys need to tell the organiser about lunch?
choices: That he wishes to skip it
That he will take it earlier
That he will bring a guest
That he does not eat meat
questions.explanation: The agenda asks participants to state dietary requirements at registration; Mr. Soltys says he is vegetarian and forgot to mention this.

questions.prompt: The word "succession" in the agenda is closest in meaning to
choices: a series of meetings in one day
who will replace leaders later
the success of a project
the order of speakers
questions.explanation: Planning for succession means preparing for who will take over leadership roles in the future.

documents.title: Rentaway Car Hire: Terms
documents.text:
RENTAWAY CAR HIRE | Rental terms

Standard rate: 42 euros per day for a compact car, including 200 kilometres a day. Each additional kilometre costs 0.25 euros.

Optional extras: full insurance at 12 euros per day; additional driver at 8 euros per day; child seat at 5 euros per day.

Young driver surcharge: drivers aged under 25 pay an extra 15 euros per day.

Fuel: cars are supplied with a full tank and must be returned full; otherwise a refuelling charge of 2.50 euros per litre missing is applied.

Late return: returns up to one hour after the agreed time are free; thereafter a full extra day is charged, at the standard rate and with the same extras. The kilometre allowance is based on the number of days charged.

Cancellation: free up to 48 hours before collection; after that, the first day's rental is charged.

Travel abroad: cars may be driven to neighbouring countries with prior notice and an additional cross-border fee of 30 euros per rental. Cars must not be driven off paved roads.

documents.text:

documents.title: Hartley Library: Temporary Closure
documents.text:
HARTLEY PUBLIC LIBRARY | NOTICE

The library will be closed to the public from Saturday 1 March to Friday 14 March inclusive, while the floors are replaced and new shelving is installed. It will reopen on Saturday 15 March at 9:00.

During the closure, books may not be returned, but the outdoor book drop will remain locked. Loans due during the closure will be automatically extended until 15 March. Late fines are charged at 25 cents per day for each overdue item, up to a maximum of 10 euros per item. No fines will accrue on days when the library is closed. Borrowers can renew items online at any time, unless another reader has reserved them.

The mobile library, which holds about 3,000 titles, will visit Marlow Square on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 14:00 to 17:00 during the closure. It cannot accept returns but can issue new loans against a valid library card. Readers who wish to join the library may register at the mobile library by presenting proof of address. We apologise for the inconvenience and thank all our readers for their patience.

documents.title: Fines for overdue books
documents.text:
14 Orchard Lane
17 March

Dear Librarian,

I am writing about the fines on my account. I had three books due on 20 February, but I was away until the end of that month, and I intended to return them on my first day back, 28 February. Unfortunately I fell ill, and by the time I was well enough to go out, the library had closed for the renovation. I returned the books on Saturday 15 March, the day it reopened. My account now shows fines of 5.75 euros for each of the three books, a total of 17.25 euros. I believe this is incorrect, since the notice said that no fines accrue while the library is closed. Would you kindly check and adjust the amount?

Yours faithfully,
Hugo Lindqvist

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Mr. Lindqvist's letter?
choices: To request a refund for a damaged book
To ask when the library will reopen
To complain about the new shelving
To contest the fines charged to him
questions.explanation: He says the fines on his account are 'incorrect' and asks the library to check and adjust them.

questions.prompt: How much should Mr. Lindqvist pay for each book?
choices: 5.75 euros
3.50 euros
2.25 euros
10 euros
questions.explanation: The books were due on 20 February and returned on 15 March, 23 days later. 14 of those days (1 to 14 March) were closure days, leaving 9 days of fines: 9 x 0.25 = 2.25 euros.

questions.prompt: How were the fines on his account apparently calculated?
choices: As if the library had been open on every day
By applying the maximum of 10 euros to each book
By counting only the days after 15 March
By charging for the weeks of the closure only
questions.explanation: The fines of 5.75 euros per book correspond to 23 days at 0.25 euros, from 20 February to 15 March, so the closure days were counted. Properly, only 9 days (2.25 euros per book, 6.75 euros in all) should be charged, a reduction of 10.50 euros.

questions.prompt: The word "accrue" in the notice is closest in meaning to
choices: be removed
be paid
be explained
build up
questions.explanation: Fines that accrue accumulate over time.

questions.prompt: What is NOT true according to the notice?
choices: Items on loan can be renewed online
The library will reopen on 15 March at 9:00
The mobile library takes returns
Loans due during the closure are extended
questions.explanation: The notice states that the mobile library 'cannot accept returns'. The other statements are in the notice.

documents.title: Westvale Foundation Scholarship
documents.text:
THE WESTVALE FOUNDATION
Scholarship for Undergraduate Study

The Foundation offers scholarships to students entering their first year at a recognised university. The awards are as follows:

A full merit scholarship of 12,000 euros per year is awarded to applicants with a grade point average (GPA) of 3.5 or above. Applicants with a GPA between 3.2 and 3.49 may receive a partial merit scholarship of 6,000 euros per year. Applicants below 3.2 are not eligible.

Any successful applicant whose household income is below 40,000 euros per year will also receive a need-based supplement of 1,500 euros per year. Awards are renewable for up to three further years, provided that the student maintains a GPA of at least 3.2 and remains enrolled full time.

Applications must include a personal statement of up to 500 words and one letter of reference. The closing date is 30 April. Decisions will be announced by 15 June.

documents.title: Bus Network to Be Redrawn from September
documents.text:
Greater Ashford's bus network will be redrawn from 1 September, the transport authority announced on Wednesday, in the first major overhaul in twenty years. The plan replaces 34 existing routes with 22 simpler ones, and concentrates services on seven corridors where buses will run at least every ten minutes between 7:00 and 19:00.

Route 14, which links the Riverside estate with the hospital, will be abolished. Passengers will instead be offered the new Route 41, which will run every ten minutes to the town centre, where they can change onto Route 7 for the hospital. The authority said that most journeys would take about the same time as at present, although some passengers will have to change buses for the first time.

Fares will be unchanged, but a new rule will allow passengers to change buses free of charge within 60 minutes. Councillor Priya Raman, who chairs the transport committee, said that the aim was "fewer routes, better frequency, and more reliable connections". A public consultation will run until 31 July, and residents may comment online or at libraries.

documents.title: Concerns about Route 14
documents.text:
To: Transport Consultation
From: Bernard Walsh
Subject: Concerns about Route 14

Dear Sir or Madam,

I live on the Riverside estate and I rely on Route 14 to reach the hospital, where I attend physiotherapy sessions twice a week after an operation. I cannot walk far and find it hard to climb steps, so changing buses in the town centre, with a wait, is a real difficulty for me. I was glad to read that the new service will run every ten minutes, but I should like to know whether the connection with Route 7 will be timed to avoid a long wait, and whether the transfer will cost me anything extra. May I also ask whether the stops in the town centre will be close to one another?

Yours faithfully,
Bernard Walsh

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Mr. Walsh's e-mail?
choices: To propose a new route for the Riverside estate
To voice his worries about the changes
To praise the plan for a simpler bus network
To report a problem with a bus driver
questions.explanation: He explains that he depends on Route 14 and asks about waiting times, cost, and the distance between stops.

questions.prompt: What is suggested about the transfer that Mr. Walsh would need to make?
choices: It would be possible only at the hospital
It would cost the same as a new single fare
It would be avoided by taking a taxi
It would be free within sixty minutes
questions.explanation: The new rule lets passengers change buses free of charge within 60 minutes.

questions.prompt: What will happen to Route 14?
choices: It will be extended through to the town centre
It will be replaced by a route with a change
It will run every ten minutes to the hospital
It will be merged into the existing Route 7 line
questions.explanation: Route 14 will be abolished; passengers go on Route 41 to the town centre and change onto Route 7 for the hospital.

questions.prompt: The word "overhaul" in the article is closest in meaning to
choices: thorough revision
minor repair
temporary closure
public complaint
questions.explanation: A major overhaul is a complete and thorough reorganisation.

questions.prompt: What is NOT stated in the article?
choices: Consultation continues until the end of July
Fares will rise to pay for the new network
Some passengers must change buses for the first time
Buses will run frequently on seven corridors
questions.explanation: The article says that fares will be unchanged. The other statements are in the text.
